findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/adr.js::adr format and native-map get newly load config, coupling their exit-0 floor to rc parseability
findings.title: adr format and native-map get newly load config, coupling their exit-0 floor to rc parseability
findings.action: None required; the premise does not hold.
findings.refutation: Isolated against the pristine ce6d0ffd baseline across valid, malformed and absent config, for both `adr format --json` and `native-map get --json`: every one of the six cells is exit 0 on baseline and exit 0 with the change. The feared exit-2 never occurs and the floor holds.
findings.disposition_rationale: The finding itself marked the loadConfig throw behaviour unverifiable from the files supplied, and it does not hold. Worth recording that my first measurement appeared to show a change: that was my own test bug, prefixing an already-absolute baseline path with $(pwd), so the apparent baseline exit 1 was node failing to find the script. The isolated re-run refutes the finding.

occurrences.title: adr format and native-map get newly load config, coupling their exit-0 floor to rc parseability

findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/native-map.js::an operator-configured templates_path is interpolated unquoted into a suggested shell command
findings.title: An operator-configured templates_path is interpolated unquoted into a suggested shell command
findings.action: Shell-quote the interpolated paths, or name them without wrapping them in a runnable command when they contain shell metacharacters.
findings.disposition_rationale: Partially valid and the one security-adjacent finding of the series. Verified by reading the sources: the resolver notices at config.js:1213 and :1217 use hardcoded directory names and are safe, so exactly one site interpolates a configured value into a backtick-quoted command. It matters more than self-inflicted because `.faffrc.yaml` is committed and shared, so a value set in a pull request could land in a command a different developer pastes. Not fixed here because the message's shape is specified and quoting changes specified user-facing output. Recorded in <run-dir>/FAFF-1300/discovered-scope.json.

occurrences.title: An operator-configured templates_path is interpolated unquoted into a suggested shell command

findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/native-map.js::dry-run with --force over a deprecated-only map does not predict the left-in-place outcome
findings.title: dry-run with --force over a deprecated-only map does not predict the left-in-place outcome
findings.action: Emit the left-in-place advisory under --dry-run, for symmetry with the spec's stated dry-run rule.
findings.disposition_rationale: Fair, and it cites the spec's own rule that each branch which would refuse or no-op a real run is an advisory under --dry-run. The refusal branches got that treatment and this outcome-bearing branch did not. Nothing is lost or mis-written; the outcome is reported post-hoc in the success output and the `deprecated_left_in_place` JSON field. Filed as a small symmetry gap. Recorded in <run-dir>/FAFF-1300/discovered-scope.json.

findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/config.js::--absolute is accepted and silently ignored on every other config sub-verb
findings.title: --absolute is accepted and silently ignored on every other config sub-verb
findings.action: Scope the flag to the verbs that honour it, so an unsupported use is refused rather than ignored.
findings.disposition_rationale: CONFIRMED by running it: `faff config get appetite --absolute` parses cleanly and prints `high`, ignoring the flag. The finding is right that this is the drift the codebase documents against, and that `native-map.js` refuses `--type` on `set` for exactly that reason. Not fixed here because the flag lives on the shared CONFIG_SPEC and scoping it means per-verb validation across the whole config surface, well outside this ticket. Recorded in <run-dir>/FAFF-1300/discovered-scope.json.

occurrences.title: --absolute is accepted and silently ignored on every other config sub-verb

findings.finding_id: test/native-map.test.mjs::the new cli test helpers spawned a path-resolved node rather than the running one
findings.title: The new CLI test helpers spawned a PATH-resolved node rather than the running one
findings.action: Spawn process.execPath, matching the sibling templates-path test.
findings.disposition_rationale: CONFIRMED and fixed in commit ceaf3e62. Both new helpers spawned the literal `node` while the sibling `test/templates-path.test.mjs` uses `process.execPath`, so on a host whose PATH node differs from the running binary the new assertions would fail for reasons unrelated to the code. Both call sites now use `process.execPath`; the three touched test files pass 62 of 62 in a clean environment.

occurrences.title: The new CLI test helpers spawned a PATH-resolved node rather than the running one
